symptom: re-running a settled script of 600 `create or modify page` statements took over 100 s where creating the pages took 29 s; memeqbody alone was 14.4 s of it, flat (ako/mxcli#2160)
cause: the decode cache of ADR-0015 recognises a unit by the bytes it was decoded from: by slice identity where it can, by bytes.Equal where it cannot. The reader's content cache lives for one pass, so the check and the exec each read into buffers of their own. On a match by comparison the cache entry kept the earlier pass's buffer, so identity never matched again in that pass and every listing compared every unit of the type: all the project's pages, twice per page statement
file: modelsdk/mprread/decode_cache.go (lookup adopts the matching buffer; DecodeCacheBytesCompared), mdl/executor/decode_cache_compare_pedapp_test.go
insight: A cost I introduced with the cache itself, invisible in every measurement made when it was added because those timed first runs and counted decodes: the cache hit, so decodes were zero and the test was green, while each hit cost a full comparison. The CPU profile showed it as memeqbody under decodeCache.lookup; the cause took a per-read log (cache on, hash known, entry present, hash equal, shared) to see that the reader was returning the same buffer every time and it was the decode cache holding a stale one. A cache keyed by content has two costs, the miss and the proof of the hit, and only the first was being counted. Measured: bytes compared for a settled 8-page re-run on PedApp 43.2 MB -> 3.5 MB (2 pages: 10.8 MB -> 2.9 MB); the 600-page settled re-run 103.7 s -> 86.8 s, output identical.
